passages.text: Overview The following overview is qualified in its entirety by the more complete discussion contained in this Item 7, the risk factors set forth in Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K, and our consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto set forth in Item 8 of this Form 10-K. Please also see the cautionary language at the beginning of Part I of this Annual Report regarding forward-looking statements. Unless otherwise noted, this Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations does not include the operations of our former Software Integrity business. See Note 3. Discontinued Operations of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in this Annual Report for additional information about the sale of our former Software Integrity business (the Software Integrity Divestiture). Fiscal 2025 Financial Performance Summary For fiscal 2025, our results reflect continued, strong execution and the resiliency of our business, including 15% revenue growth compared to fiscal 2024, primarily due to revenue growth across a majority of product groups and geographies and the closing of the Ansys Merger, which contributed $756.6 million in revenue, which was offset by weakness in our business in China, which saw revenue decrease 22% compared to fiscal 2024, excluding Ansys. We saw strength in our Design Automation segment, including strong demand for our hardware products. This was offset by weakness in our Design IP segment, due to several headwinds, including China export control restrictions, such as the Q3 2025 BIS Restrictions (as defined below), which disrupted customer design starts in China, weaker than expected demand from a major foundry customer, and certain roadmap and resource decisions that did not yield their intended results. We have begun taking actions to sharpen our execution and reallocate resources to the highest growth opportunities in our Design IP segment, but expect to see muted growth in fiscal 2026. Any significant disruption caused by these or other geopolitical pressures or conflicts could materially affect our employees, business, operating results, financial condition or customers in those regions of the world. For example, Synopsys has employees, operations, customers and strategic partners in the Middle East. While we are actively monitoring the conflicts in the Middle East, at this time they have not had a material impact on our business, operating results or financial condition to date. Business Segments Design Automation. This segment includes our advanced silicon design, verification products and services, and Ansys products, and system integration products and services. This segment also includes digital, custom and field programmable gate array (FPGA) integrated circuit (IC) design software, verification software and hardware products, and manufacturing software products. Designers use our EDA products to accelerate and automate the chip design process, reduce errors and enable more powerful and robust designs, with improved productivity for faster time to market. Engineers use our S&A solutions to virtually test and optimize designs across various physics domains, such as structural analysis, thermal analysis, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Design IP. This segment includes our interface, foundation, security, and embedded processor IP, IP subsystems, and IP implementation services that serve companies primarily in the semiconductor and electronics industries. We are a leading provider of high-quality, silicon-proven IP solutions for system-on-chips (SoCs). This includes IP that has been optimized to address specific application requirements for the mobile, automotive, digital home, Internet of Things and AI/data center markets, enabling designers to quickly develop SoCs in these areas. Fiscal Year End We have changed our fiscal year end from the Saturday nearest to October 31 and consisting of 52 or 53 fiscal weeks to a fiscal year end of October 31 each year. The fiscal year change became effective with our fiscal 2025, which began on November 3, 2024. Our fiscal quarters end on January 31, April 30, July 31 and October 31 of each year. Historically, our fiscal years have been 52- or 53-week periods ending on the Saturday nearest to October 31. Fiscal 2024 was a 53-week year ended on November 2, 2024. Fiscal 2023 was a 52-week year ended on October 28, 2023. The extra week in the first quarter of fiscal 2024 resulted in approximately $63.2 million of additional revenue, and approximately $52.5 million of additional expenses, including approximately $10.6 million in stock-based compensation costs from continuing operations. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably exceeds buybacks, and free cash flow after capital expenditure remains solidly positive, giving the issuer genuine internal funding capacity despite the debt taken on for the Ansys Merger. Cash generation is the core support for the capital structure.

The current ratio sits above one and comfortably covers near-term liabilities, and the Altman Z double prime zone is safe, indicating the balance sheet retains a liquidity cushion even after the transformational acquisition closed during the year.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage sits far above the sector median and rose sharply year on year as debt jumped from a negligible base to fund the Ansys Merger. Net leverage on a cash-and-investments basis is also many times the sector median, placing the issuer in the highly leveraged band.

Disclosed risk factors flag export control and geopolitical exposure, notably China restrictions that disrupted design starts and drove a sharp China revenue decline, with muted Design IP growth expected ahead. This concentration threatens the revenue base underpinning deleveraging.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage fell well below the prior year and the sector median, and EBITDA coverage is similarly weak against peers. Operating income now covers interest only modestly, so servicing depends on sustaining earnings as merger-related interest costs bite.

Free cash flow to debt and operating cash flow to debt both sit far below sector medians, reflecting the enlarged debt stack. Cash flow covers net debt only marginally above the next risk-band boundary, leaving limited headroom before a cashflow downgrade.

overall_credit_view.text: The credit profile is highly leveraged on an indicative basis, with leverage and coverage metrics well outside sector norms following the debt-funded Ansys Merger. Deleveraging hinges on EBITDA recovery and disciplined capital allocation rather than on further borrowing capacity.

The maturity ladder concentrates repayments in the intermediate years with a large tail beyond year five, so refinancing risk is manageable near term but meaningful later. Our view is that sustained free cash flow and stable margins are needed to meet those maturities without reliance on market access.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流穩健地超過回購金額，扣除資本開支後的自由現金流仍穩健地維持正數，儘管因收購Ansys而承擔債務，發行人仍具備真正的內部融資能力。現金產生是資本結構的核心支撐。
流動比率高於一，並穩健地覆蓋短期負債，而Altman Z double prime區域處於安全水平，顯示即使年內完成該項轉型性收購後，資產負債表仍保留流動性緩衝。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿遠高於行業中位數，並按年大幅上升，因債務由微不足道的基數躍升以撥付Ansys收購。按現金及投資計算的淨槓桿亦為行業中位數的多倍，使發行人處於高槓桿區間。
披露的風險因素指出出口管制及地緣政治風險敞口，尤其是中國限制措施干擾設計啟動並導致中國收入大幅下降，預期未來Design IP增長疲弱。此集中度威脅支撐去槓桿的收入基礎。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率遠低於上年及行業中位數，而EBITDA覆蓋率相對於同業亦同樣疲弱。經營溢利現時僅勉強覆蓋利息，因此償債能力取決於能否在併購相關利息成本造成壓力下維持盈利。
自由現金流對債務及營運現金流對債務均遠低於行業中位數，反映擴大的債務規模。現金流僅勉強覆蓋淨債務至高於下一風險區間邊界，在現金流降級前留下的緩衝有限。

overall_credit_view.text: 按指示性基準，信貸狀況屬高槓桿，在債務融資的Ansys收購後，槓桿及覆蓋指標均遠超行業常態。去槓桿取決於EBITDA復甦及嚴謹的資本配置，而非進一步的借貸能力。
到期結構將還款集中於中期年份，並在五年後有龐大的尾部，因此再融資風險短期內可控，但後期則具實質意義。我們認為需要持續的自由現金流及穩定的利潤率，才能在不依賴市場准入的情況下應付該等到期債務。
